page.title: The front door against its own source
page.standfirst_html: Every flag the comparator raised for index.qmd, adjudicated against A.PLEASE.START.HERE.08Feb22.pdf — the second source #803 discovered, and like the Welcome booklet one with no page images in the repo, so all 22 were rendered for this pass. The headline is that the file's first two sections were copy-edited and the other seven were not. The Preface and “Active learning” carry 16 punctuation changes the source does not have — stops moved inside quotation marks, i.e. becoming i.e.,, six inserted commas — while a word-level diff of everything after them returns nothing but correct italics. The site's own corpus settles it: i.e. 200 against i.e., 5, and four of the seven corpus-wide outliers sit in this one section. Two substantive Preface findings ride with them: a silent grammar fix (justify → justifies) and a parenthetical stripped of its commas. Separately, an already-logged deviation removed three sentences about the clock icons, but two of the three do not depend on the icons — they explain the timings, which the site still carries on 44 chapters as ~ M min at Neave's pace, derived from those very clocks. All 30 missing paragraphs and all 4 unsourced ones resolve to existing deviations.

sections.title: Fix proposed

They are split by class so they can be taken separately, but they stand or fall together. I-23 was raised after the first decision round, by the post-fix validator re-run, and decided in a second export.

items.evidence_html: Already covered by docs/deviations/2026-04-28-remove-decorative-clock-icons-and-the-welcome-page-paragraph.md (#286 / PR #288), which removed these alongside the clock SVGs. The finding is that it over-removed against its own rationale. Only the first sentence depends on the icons; the other two describe how to treat the timings. That deviation says “the chapter-top reading-time indicator (filters/reading-time.lua) already conveys actionable pacing” — and it does, as ~ N min reading · ~ M min at Neave's pace, where M is session_minutes, derived from the very clocks that were removed, on 44 chapters. create_clock now appears in 0 content files. So the mechanism survived and only Neave's guidance on it was lost, leaving the site's timings explained nowhere. Proposed as an adapted restoration — the icon sentence stays removed — which needs its own deviations entry amending the 2026-04-28 one.
items.decision_note: "Each chapter opens with an indication of the time Neave allowed for it" should be written in the first (i.e. as if from Neave), or else formatted as an editorial note
items.outcome: Restored in adapted form, rewritten into Neave's first person per Lee's note; the 2026-04-28 clock deviation is amended by docs/deviations/2026-09-12-index-timing-guidance-restored.md.
